criteria.note: THE HEADLINE FAILS, AND THE REVIEWER PROVED IT BY MUTATION RATHER THAN BY READING. The assertion that exists is real (_sleep is time.sleep, _clock is time.monotonic, _record is None, with a negative control that is False for a fake waiter) but it constructs a SettleWaiter, NOT a runner. Production never constructs one: main() calls run(journey, driver, outdir) with no waiter, and run / apply_step / redrive each resolve `if waiter is None: waiter = SettleWaiter()`. Those three resolution sites are asserted by NOTHING. The reviewer edited all SEVEN shipped copies of the android runner to `waiter = SettleWaiter(sleep=lambda s: None)` at those sites - an adopter running the shipped runner would then do ZERO waiting on every launch, tap, text, key, wait and every lifecycle re-drive - and the full selftest reported 3261 passed, 0 failed. Byte-restored afterwards with the sha re-verified. So the exact outcome the spec calls 'the worst outcome available here' is reachable with the gate GREEN. AC1's own sentence describes a test that does not exist.

The substance is verified and the wording is false. CONSTANTS: PASS, independently verified by parsing both runners with ast at the parent and the child and comparing the ORDERED duration lists - android 13 old / 13 new with identical durations, iOS 10 old / 10 new with identical durations, 23 routed, multisets and order identical, nothing shortened in either direction, step overrides preserved at every site that had one, the two raw android driver sleeps surviving untouched while iOS now has zero raw time.sleep calls, all 7 copies of each runner byte-identical and process_runner.py byte-unchanged across all 7. THE CRITERION'S OWN SENTENCE IS FALSE: 'THE CRITERION IS THEREFORE 23 ROUTED CALLS ON 21 LINES'. Measured at the parent, the 23 routed calls sat on NINETEEN lines (android 10, iOS 9). 21 is the count of ALL sleep-bearing lines, which includes the two android driver lines carrying the condition waits AC2 itself says are NOT routed. In the new source those 23 calls sit on 23 lines.

REAL, AND NOT A STAND-IN. The recorder logs (reason, seconds, t0, t1); the whole ordered sequence is compared to a frozen expectation per module; process_death is additionally pinned as an explicit slice (terminate then launch); and a coherence assertion (t1 minus t0 equals seconds, now equals the running sum) proves the time came from the INJECTED pair. The two remaining raw waits really are condition waits (AdbDriver.wait_boot's sys.boot_completed poll, and stop_recording's flush before pulling the file) and were correctly left out of the seam.

AC4's sentence 'the full gate is GREEN' is FALSE at the reviewed commit: the gate is RED on two stages. The manifest is honest about this and marks AC4 not_measured_yet, so it is AC4's sentence in the spec that is false rather than the manifest. Separately the reviewer measured the timing AC4 leaves unmeasured and found the saving real: selftest 191.57s and 190.19s at the parent, 145.84s and 145.81s at the child, a median delta of about 45.7s against the derived 46.0, corroborated to within about one percent on a box at load 0.5 to 1.2.

findings.text: PROVEN: A FAKE DEFAULT AT THE RUNNER'S OWN RESOLUTION SITES SURVIVES THE SUITE. `waiter = SettleWaiter(sleep=lambda s: None)` in run / apply_step / redrive, applied to all 7 shipped android copies, leaves selftest at 3261 passed / 0 failed. Adopter waiting is gone and nothing reddens. This is the forbidden 'default to a fake clock in production'. THE FIX IS CHEAP AND COUNT-FREE, and the reviewer named it: an AST universal that EVERY SettleWaiter( construction inside each runner module carries zero args and zero keywords, composed with the existing identity check, plus a mutant proving it fires.

PROVEN: THE INJECTION-SITE AST CHECK MATCHES ONLY AR.run(...) AND IOS.run(...) ON THOSE TWO EXACT NAMES. Run over synthetic sources it MISSES mod.run(J, drv, d) - the very form the block's own _v13_drive helper uses internally - MISSES _v13_drive("android", J, d), whose own waiter=None default silently restores wall time, MISSES an alias M = AR; M.run(...), and MISSES a dict lookup _V13_MODS['android'].run(...). So the item's stated likeliest silent regression is open through the helper this block itself defines.

PROVEN: THE 'NO REAL SLEEP LEAKS' PROBE IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THAT SAME REGRESSION. It swaps the time.sleep MODULE ATTRIBUTE, but SettleWaiter.__init__'s default is bound at def time to the function OBJECT. The reviewer constructed SettleWaiter() with the wrapper installed and the wrapper never fired (w._sleep is the real time.sleep: True; is the patched attribute: False). A dropped waiter therefore sleeps for real and is charged to nobody. The negative control cannot expose this, because it calls time.sleep through the module attribute, which is the one path the wrapper can see.

FALSE SENTENCES, EACH MEASURED, TO DELETE RATHER THAN SOFTEN. (a) the spec's AC2, the rollback paragraph, the manifest's AC2 evidence and the dogfood assertion that pins it all carry 'ON 21 LINES', which was NINETEEN at the parent. (b) the spec's AC1 describes a test that does not exist. (c) the spec's AC4 says the full gate is GREEN and it is RED. (d) the INJECTION SITES assertion claims 'it is a UNIVERSAL over whatever drive sites exist rather than an assertion that there are ten, so a new one added tomorrow is covered too' - disproven for three call forms; delete the 'covered too' clause. (e) the T1 assertion and the identical claim shipped in BOTH runners' SettleWaiter docstrings say a condition wait is 'inexpressible in this API' and 'cannot be expressed in this API at all'; a poll IS expressible as settle-in-a-loop, which is exactly why T3 exists. State the true weaker thing: the API offers no predicate, deadline or poll primitive, so a condition wait cannot be expressed DIRECTLY. (f) the T3 assertion says 'a POLL cannot be built on top of the seam'; it cannot be built LEXICALLY INSIDE A LOOP BODY, and the consequence as written overstates a lexical check.

T1 AND T3 ARE LEXICAL, SO A CONDITION WAIT CAN BE BUILT ON THE SEAM: `while not p(): _one_settle()` with the settle in a module-level helper is caught by neither, because T3 only finds a settle lexically inside a For or While body and run() already calls apply_step from a for loop.

LATE BINDING, MINOR BUT WORTH KNOWING and the same mechanism as the probe blindness: the runners previously looked time.sleep up dynamically, so an adopter harness (or gevent-style patching) applied after import intercepted the waits; it no longer does. 'Behaviour outside the gate is byte-identical' holds for wall-clock waiting, NOT for interception.

ACCEPTED RATHER THAN RAISED, and correctly disclosed in the item's known_limits: the frozen table, the AST map and AC2's text all move together if one builder edits all three in one commit. The enumerated numbers in AC2 are the real defence.
